question: Who among the following won the award of the best actor at the 71st National Film Awards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Rukh Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 71st National Film Awards (for films of 2023, announced in August 2025), the Best Actor (सर्वश्रेष्ठ अभिनेता) award was jointly won by Shah Rukh Khan for his role in *Jawan* and Vikrant Massey for *12th Fail*.

• This was Shah Rukh Khan's first-ever National Film Award for Best Actor in his decades-long career.

• The National Film Awards (राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कार) are presented annually by the Directorate of Film Festivals under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rani Mukerji won the Best Actress award (for *Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway*) at the 71st National Film Awards.

• Mohanlal was conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the highest honour in Indian cinema, at the same ceremony.

• The awards were presented by the President of India in New Delhi.

NOTE

• Ranbir Kapoor (Option 1): A leading Bollywood actor known for films like *Barfi!*, *Sanju* and *Animal*; he was not the Best Actor at the 71st National Film Awards.

• Vikrant Massey (Option 2): Co-winner of the Best Actor award for *12th Fail*, sharing the honour with Shah Rukh Khan; the key marks Shah Rukh Khan as the answer.

• Ayushmann Khurrana (Option 4): A National Award-winning actor (for *Andhadhun*, 2018) but not a recipient at the 71st edition.

question: In March 2025, who has been appointed as the Chairman of the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashok Singh Thakur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In March 2025, Ashok Singh Thakur was elected as the Chairman of INTACH — the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कला एवं सांस्कृतिक विरासत न्यास).

• He is a retired IAS officer and former Union Secretary; he succeeded the previous chairman at INTACH.

• INTACH is a non-profit organisation founded in 1984 in New Delhi to protect and conserve India's natural and cultural heritage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• INTACH works in areas such as heritage conservation, documentation, education and awareness across India.

• It has chapters spread across the country and internationally, making it one of the world's largest heritage organisations.

• Its headquarters are located in New Delhi.

NOTE

• Virat Sunil Diwanji (Option 2): Not associated with the chairmanship of INTACH; a distractor name.

• Manish Tiwary (Option 3): Not the appointee; used as a distractor in the question.

• Aviral Jain (Option 4): Not connected to the INTACH chairmanship; a distractor option.

question: Sanjiv Ranjan has been appointed as Secretary-General of the Indian Ocean Rim Association Secretariat in Mauritius on 1st January 2025 for a term of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanjiv Ranjan assumed charge as the Secretary-General of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Secretariat in Mauritius on 1st January 2025 for a three-year term (तीन वर्ष का कार्यकाल).

• He is an Indian diplomat (IFS officer) taking over the top administrative post of the IORA.

• IORA is an inter-governmental organisation established in 1997 to promote regional cooperation among Indian Ocean rim countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• IORA has its Secretariat headquartered in Ebène, Mauritius.

• It currently has 23 Member States and several Dialogue Partners; India is a founding member.

• IORA works on maritime safety, trade facilitation, fisheries management, disaster risk management and the blue economy.

NOTE

• 2 years (Option 1): Not the tenure of the Secretary-General; a distractor value.

• 4 years (Option 3): Incorrect term length for this appointment.

• 5 years (Option 4): Not the term specified for Sanjiv Ranjan's appointment.

question: In May 2025, the Supreme Court set aside which High Court order that had denied maternity leave to a government school teacher for the birth of their third child?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madras High Court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2025, the Supreme Court set aside a Madras High Court (मद्रास उच्च न्यायालय) order that had denied maternity leave (मातृत्व अवकाश) to a government school teacher for the birth of her third child.

• The Supreme Court held that maternity leave is part of a woman's reproductive rights and dignity, and cannot be denied merely because of the number of children.

• The Court emphasised that reproductive rights and the right to maternity benefits fall within the ambit of Article 21 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Madras High Court is the High Court of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, established in 1862, and is one of the three oldest High Courts in India.

• Maternity benefits in India are governed by the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (amended in 2017).

• The 2017 amendment increased paid maternity leave from 12 weeks to 26 weeks for the first two children.

NOTE

• Delhi High Court (Option 2): Not the High Court whose order was set aside in this case.

• Calcutta High Court (Option 3): The oldest High Court in India (1862) but not involved in this ruling.

• Bombay High Court (Option 4): Not connected to this particular maternity leave order.

question: As of December 2024, _______ million women in India were monitoring their credit, signalling growing financial awareness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of December 2024, about 27 million women (2.7 करोड़ महिलाएं) in India were actively monitoring their credit, reflecting rising financial awareness (वित्तीय जागरूकता) among women.

• This growth points to increasing participation of women in the formal credit and financial system.

• Credit monitoring helps individuals track their credit scores and improve access to loans and financial products.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Credit information in India is maintained by credit bureaus such as CIBIL (TransUnion CIBIL), Experian, Equifax and CRIF High Mark.

• A good credit score typically ranges between 750 and 900 and improves loan eligibility.

• Government schemes and digital lending have expanded women's access to formal credit.

NOTE

• 51 (Option 2): An overstated figure; not the reported number of women monitoring credit.

• 42 (Option 3): Incorrect value used as a distractor.

• 36 (Option 4): Not the figure reported for December 2024.

question: Which scheme of the Central Government aims to empower artisans with ₹500 stipend/day and toolkit vouchers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Vishwakarma Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The PM Vishwakarma Scheme (पीएम विश्वकर्मा योजना) aims to empower traditional artisans and craftspeople by providing a stipend of ₹500 per day during skill training and a toolkit incentive (voucher) of ₹15,000.

• It was launched on 17 September 2023 (Vishwakarma Jayanti) by the Government of India.

• The scheme covers 18 traditional trades such as carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters and cobblers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Beneficiaries receive collateral-free credit up to ₹1 lakh (first tranche) and ₹2 lakh (second tranche) at a concessional interest rate of 5%.

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME).

• Recipients get PM Vishwakarma certificates and ID cards recognising their identity as artisans.

NOTE

• PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (Option 2): Provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments to eligible farmer families, not artisans.

• NPS Vatsalya (Option 3): A pension savings scheme launched in 2024 that allows parents to invest for their minor children.

• PM SVANidhi (Option 4): A micro-credit scheme providing working capital loans to street vendors.

question: Which Indian state topped the Fiscal Health Index 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Odisha (ओडिशा) topped the Fiscal Health Index (FHI) 2025, released by NITI Aayog, with the highest overall index score.

• The FHI assessed the fiscal performance of 18 major states based on the 2022-23 financial data.

• Odisha excelled in the Debt Index and Debt Sustainability, reflecting strong financial governance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Fiscal Health Index was released for the first time by NITI Aayog in January 2025.

• It evaluates states on five sub-indices: Quality of Expenditure, Revenue Mobilisation, Fiscal Prudence, Debt Index and Debt Sustainability.

• States such as Chhattisgarh and Goa followed Odisha near the top, while Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and West Bengal were among the laggards.

NOTE

• Haryana (Option 2): A well-performing state but not the topper of the Fiscal Health Index 2025.

• Goa (Option 3): Ranked among the top states but did not top the index (this option was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Not the top-ranked state in the FHI 2025.

question: The Hesaraghatta grasslands are in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengaluru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hesaraghatta grasslands (हेसरघट्टा घास के मैदान) are located near Bengaluru in Karnataka.

• In 2024, the Karnataka government declared the area as the Greater Hesaraghatta Grassland Conservation Reserve.

• It is one of the last remaining grassland ecosystems near Bengaluru and a rich habitat for birds and wildlife.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The reserve spans over 5,000 acres and supports species like the lesser florican, leopards and numerous migratory birds.

• Hesaraghatta also has a historic lake built in 1894 across the Arkavathi river to supply water to Bengaluru.

• Grasslands are important carbon sinks and vital for biodiversity conservation.

NOTE

• Mumbai (Option 2): The capital of Maharashtra; not the location of the Hesaraghatta grasslands.

• Hyderabad (Option 3): The capital of Telangana; unrelated to Hesaraghatta.

• Bhopal (Option 4): The capital of Madhya Pradesh; not linked to these grasslands.

question: As per the "EnviStats India 2024: Environment Accounts", the coverage of Mangroves has increased around _____ percent over the years 2013 to 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per "EnviStats India 2024: Environment Accounts", the coverage of mangroves (मैंग्रोव) in India increased by around 8 percent over the years 2013 to 2021.

• EnviStats India is published by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• Mangroves act as natural coastal barriers, protecting against cyclones, erosion and tsunamis.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mangroves are salt-tolerant vegetation found in coastal intertidal zones.

• The Sundarbans in West Bengal is the largest mangrove forest in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Mangroves are important blue carbon ecosystems, storing large amounts of carbon.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Understates the reported increase in mangrove coverage.

• 40 (Option 3): A greatly exaggerated figure; not supported by EnviStats data.

• 65 (Option 4): Far too high a value for the mangrove coverage increase.

question: Which among the following is a wind instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pava.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pava is a wind instrument (सुषिर वाद्य यंत्र) — a type of flute traditionally associated with folk music, notably in Goa.

• Wind instruments (Sushir Vadya) produce sound when air is blown through them.

• Other Indian wind instruments include the flute (bansuri), shehnai, nadaswaram and been.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Indian musical instruments are classified into four categories: Tata Vadya (string), Sushir Vadya (wind), Avanaddha Vadya (membrane/percussion) and Ghana Vadya (solid/idiophones).

• The Pava flute is played in Goan folk traditions such as the Dekhni dance.

• Wind instruments rely on vibrating air columns to generate musical notes.

NOTE

• Dhol (Option 1): A double-headed drum, i.e., a percussion (membrane/Avanaddha) instrument, not a wind instrument.

• Manjira (Option 3): Small hand cymbals — an idiophone (Ghana Vadya), not a wind instrument (this was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• Nagara (Option 4): A kettle-drum, i.e., a percussion (membrane) instrument, not a wind instrument.

question: What was the main function of 'Chaityas' in Buddhist architecture?
option_4: Congregational halls for teaching and interaction
solution_text:
The correct answer is Congregational halls for teaching and interaction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chaityas (चैत्य) were prayer or congregational halls in Buddhist architecture, used for worship, teaching and community gatherings.

• A chaitya typically housed a stupa at its apsidal (rounded) end, which was the object of veneration.

• Famous rock-cut chaityas are found at Karle, Bhaja, Ajanta and Ellora.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In contrast, Viharas were the residential quarters (monasteries) where Buddhist monks lived.

• The chaitya at Karle (Maharashtra) is one of the largest and finest rock-cut chaitya halls in India.

• Chaityas usually feature a horseshoe-shaped (chaitya) window and rows of pillars.

NOTE

• Living quarters for monks (Option 1): This describes a Vihara, not a chaitya (this was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• Storehouses for grains (Option 2): Not a function of chaityas; they were places of worship.

• Decorative gateways to monasteries (Option 3): Ornamental gateways were called toranas, not chaityas.

question: Which Indian state is known for the folk dance 'Dekhni'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dekhni (देखनी) is a semi-classical folk dance of Goa, performed traditionally by women.

• It blends Indian and Western (Portuguese-influenced) musical elements, reflecting Goa's cultural fusion.

• The dance is usually performed to melodious songs with graceful movements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Goa include Fugdi, Dhalo, Ghode Modni, Corridinho and Mando.

• Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961 and became a full-fledged state in 1987.

• Goa is the smallest Indian state by area.

NOTE

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Chhau, Paika and Jhumar, not Dekhni.

• Haryana (Option 3): Famous for folk dances such as Ghoomar, Phag and Dhamal.

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Known for Kathak, Raslila and Charkula, not Dekhni.

question: On October 4, 2024, the MACE telescope was officially inaugurated. Where did this event take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hanle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 4 October 2024, the MACE (Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment) telescope was inaugurated at Hanle (हान्ले) in Ladakh.

• Located at about 4,300 metres altitude, it is the highest imaging Cherenkov telescope in the world.

• It is the largest such telescope in Asia, built indigenously by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The MACE telescope is used to study high-energy gamma rays from cosmic sources.

• It was inaugurated by the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission during the Platinum Jubilee year of the Department of Atomic Energy.

• Hanle also hosts the Indian Astronomical Observatory and the country's first Dark Sky Reserve.

NOTE

• Gangtok (Option 1): The capital of Sikkim; not the site of the MACE telescope.

• Visakhapatnam (Option 3): A port city in Andhra Pradesh; unrelated to MACE.

• Jorhat (Option 4): A city in Assam; not connected to the MACE telescope.

question: In 2024, which newly discovered 'mini-moon' was expected to orbit Earth for about two months?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2024 PT5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2024, a small asteroid named 2024 PT5 was temporarily captured by Earth's gravity, acting as a 'mini-moon' (मिनी-मून).

• It was expected to orbit Earth for about two months (roughly late September to late November 2024).

• 2024 PT5 belongs to the Arjuna asteroid belt, a group of near-Earth objects with orbits similar to Earth's.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A mini-moon is a small object temporarily gravitationally bound to Earth before escaping back into a solar orbit.

• 2024 PT5 was discovered in August 2024 using the ATLAS (Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System) survey.

• It was too small and faint to be seen with the naked eye or ordinary telescopes.

NOTE

• Aditya (Option 1): Refers to ISRO's Aditya-L1 solar mission, not a mini-moon.

• Cassini (Option 2): A famous NASA-ESA spacecraft that studied Saturn; not a mini-moon.

• 2024 Rosetta (Option 4): A distractor; Rosetta was an ESA comet mission, not this asteroid.

question: In 2002-2003, the Government of India set up a committee to review the fiscal reforms both in respect of Direct and Indirect taxes under the chairmanship of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijay Kelkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2002-2003, the Government of India set up task forces to review fiscal reforms in Direct and Indirect taxes (प्रत्यक्ष और अप्रत्यक्ष कर) under the chairmanship of Vijay Kelkar.

• The Kelkar Committee/Task Force recommended major reforms in the tax structure to simplify and rationalise taxation.

• Vijay Kelkar is a noted Indian economist who also chaired the committee that gave the roadmap for the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vijay Kelkar later served as Chairman of the 13th Finance Commission and as an adviser to the Finance Ministry.

• The Kelkar Task Force recommendations influenced the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003.

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan for his contributions to public policy.

NOTE

• Chakravarthi Rangarajan (Option 2): A former RBI Governor and Chairman of the PM's Economic Advisory Council; not the chair of this task force.

• Abid Hussain (Option 3): An economist and diplomat associated with the small-scale industries committee, not this tax reform task force.

• Deepak Parekh (Option 4): A banker (HDFC chairman) known for various government advisory committees, but not this one.

question: Which of the following policies were devised by Lord Dalhousie?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Doctrine of Lapse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Doctrine of Lapse (विलय नीति) was an annexation policy devised and applied by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.

• Under it, if a ruler died without a natural (biological) heir, his adopted son could not inherit, and the state would 'lapse' to the British East India Company.

• States annexed under this policy included Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, Sambalpur and Jaitpur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The annexation of Jhansi under this doctrine made Rani Lakshmibai a key figure in the Revolt of 1857.

• Dalhousie also annexed Awadh (Oudh) in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance.

• He introduced the railways, telegraph and postal reforms in India.

NOTE

• Policy of Paramountcy (Option 2): Associated with Lord Hastings, asserting British supremacy over Indian states.

• Subsidiary Alliance (Option 3): Introduced by Lord Wellesley (1798), under which Indian rulers accepted British forces and control.

• Policy of Non-intervention (Option 4): A general policy of not interfering in the internal affairs of Indian states; not Dalhousie's annexationist doctrine.

question: In which year did the National Stock Exchange began its operations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1994.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Stock Exchange (NSE) began its operations in 1994.

• It started trading in the wholesale debt market segment in June 1994 and in the equities (capital market) segment in November 1994.

• NSE was incorporated in 1992 and recognised as a stock exchange in 1993.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NSE was India's first fully automated, screen-based electronic trading exchange.

• Its benchmark index is the NIFTY 50, comprising 50 large-cap companies.

• NSE is headquartered in Mumbai and is regulated by SEBI.

NOTE

• 1998 (Option 2): Incorrect; NSE was already operational by then.

• 2002 (Option 3): Much later than NSE's actual start of operations.

• 1996 (Option 4): The year the NIFTY index was introduced, not when NSE began operations.

question: In the context of Mineral distribution of India, which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the "South-Western Plateau region" Belt?
option_1: It covers Karnataka, Goa and contiguous Tamil Nadu uplands and Kerala.
option_2: This belt is rich in ferrous metals and bauxite.
option_3: It contains high grade iron ore.
option_4: This belt has huge amount of coal reserves.
solution_text:
The correct answer is This belt has huge amount of coal reserves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The statement that the South-Western Plateau belt 'has huge amount of coal reserves' is INCORRECT (गलत कथन) — this belt is poor in coal (except a small deposit at Neyveli lignite).

• The South-Western Plateau belt covers Karnataka, Goa, and the contiguous uplands of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

• It is rich in ferrous metals, bauxite and high-grade iron ore.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India's major mineral belts are the North-Eastern Plateau belt, South-Western Plateau belt, North-Western belt and the South-Eastern (Chhota Nagpur) belt.

• The Chhota Nagpur plateau (North-Eastern belt) is the richest in coal reserves (Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh).

• The South-Western belt also holds deposits of manganese, limestone and garnet.

NOTE

• It covers Karnataka, Goa and contiguous Tamil Nadu uplands and Kerala (Option 1): A CORRECT statement about the belt's geographic coverage.

• This belt is rich in ferrous metals and bauxite (Option 2): A CORRECT statement; the belt is indeed rich in these (this was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• It contains high grade iron ore (Option 3): A CORRECT statement, as the belt has high-grade iron ore deposits.

question:
What was the reason for the disruption in Third five year Plan?
I. Indo-Pakistan Conflict.
II. Two successive years of drought.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) was disrupted by both the Indo-Pakistan conflict (भारत-पाकिस्तान संघर्ष) and two successive years of drought.

• The India-China War (1962) and the Indo-Pak War (1965) diverted resources towards defence.

• Severe droughts and a food crisis further derailed the plan's targets, so both statements are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Third Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model and aimed to make the economy 'self-reliant and self-generating'.

• Its failure led to a Plan Holiday from 1966 to 1969, when three Annual Plans were implemented.

• Devaluation of the rupee also occurred during this period (1966).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete; the drought (Statement II) was also a major cause (this was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete; the Indo-Pak conflict (Statement I) also disrupted the plan.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both factors genuinely disrupted the Third Plan.

question: What was the growth target for twelfth five year plan in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-2017) had a growth target of 8% (revised down from the initially proposed 9%).

• Its theme was 'Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth' (तीव्र, अधिक समावेशी और सतत विकास).

• It was the last Five Year Plan of India before the planning process was replaced by NITI Aayog.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

• Manmohan Singh was the Prime Minister (ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission) when the plan began.

• India's Five Year Plans were based on the Soviet model, first launched in 1951.

NOTE

• 2% (Option 1): Far too low to be the growth target of any Five Year Plan.

• 5% (Option 2): Not the target set for the Twelfth Plan (this was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• 13% (Option 4): An unrealistically high figure; not the Twelfth Plan's target.

question: As per September 2024, according to the Ministry of External Affairs in India, there are _____ million Indians residing abroad who are either NRIs or OCIs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 32.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per September 2024, the Ministry of External Affairs (विदेश मंत्रालय) stated there are about 32 million Indians residing abroad who are either NRIs (Non-Resident Indians) or OCIs (Overseas Citizens of India).

• This makes the Indian diaspora one of the largest in the world.

• The diaspora contributes significantly to India through remittances, investment and cultural links.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India is consistently the world's largest recipient of remittances.

• NRIs are Indian citizens living abroad, while OCIs are foreign nationals of Indian origin holding a lifelong visa.

• The Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is celebrated on 9 January to mark the contribution of the overseas Indian community.

NOTE

• 44 (Option 2): Overstates the reported diaspora figure.

• 52 (Option 3): Too high a value; not the MEA figure for September 2024.

• 61 (Option 4): Far exceeds the actual number of NRIs and OCIs reported.

question: Mission Parivar Vikas was initially in the _____ high focus states.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mission Parivar Vikas (मिशन परिवार विकास) was initially launched in 2016 in 7 high focus states with a high Total Fertility Rate (TFR).

• These states were Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Assam.

• It focused on 146 high-fertility districts to improve access to contraceptives and family planning services.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

• Its main aim is to improve family planning and reduce the TFR to the replacement level of 2.1.

• It introduced new contraceptives like Antara (injectable) and Chhaya (pill).

NOTE

• 4 (Option 1): Fewer than the actual number of high focus states covered initially.

• 6 (Option 3): Incorrect; Mission Parivar Vikas began in 7, not 6, states.

• 9 (Option 4): Overstates the initial number of high focus states.

question: In which cell is the respiratory pigment haemoglobin found in humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red blood cells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The respiratory pigment haemoglobin (हीमोग्लोबिन) is found in the Red Blood Cells (RBCs / erythrocytes) in humans.

• Haemoglobin is an iron-containing protein that binds oxygen and transports it from the lungs to the tissues.

• It gives blood its characteristic red colour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mature human RBCs lack a nucleus and are biconcave in shape, increasing surface area for gas exchange.

• RBCs are produced in the bone marrow and have a lifespan of about 120 days.

• Haemoglobin also carries some carbon dioxide back to the lungs.

NOTE

• Blood platelets (Option 2): Cell fragments (thrombocytes) that help in blood clotting, not oxygen transport.

• Monocytes (Option 3): A type of white blood cell involved in immunity and phagocytosis, not carrying haemoglobin.

• Nerve cells (Option 4): Neurons that transmit electrical impulses; they do not contain haemoglobin.

question: How do plants convey information about a touch from one cell to another?
solution_text:
The correct answer is By using electrical-chemical signals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Plants convey information about a touch from one cell to another by using electrical-chemical signals (विद्युत-रासायनिक संकेत).

• Unlike animals, plants do not have a nervous system, yet they respond to stimuli through changes in the electrical potential and chemical messengers across cell membranes.

• A classic example is Mimosa pudica (touch-me-not), whose leaves fold on being touched.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The folding movement in plants like Mimosa results from changes in the turgor pressure of cells at the base of leaves (pulvinus).

• Plant responses to touch are called thigmonasty / thigmotropism.

• Plant hormones (phytohormones) such as auxins also coordinate responses to stimuli.

NOTE

• Through specialized nerve tissue (Option 1): Incorrect; plants lack nerves and nervous tissue (this was the candidate's incorrect selection).

• By producing sound waves (Option 2): Not the mechanism plants use to relay touch information.

• Through changing colour of leaves (Option 4): Colour change is not how plants transmit touch signals between cells.

question: 'Taxila', the famous centre of learning, was the capital of which Mahajanapada in ancient India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Taxila (तक्षशिला), the famous ancient centre of learning, was the capital of the Gandhara Mahajanapada.

• Gandhara was one of the 16 Mahajanapadas of ancient India, located in the north-west (present-day north-western Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan).
